correctness.rationale: Alexeev--Cahill--Mixon's prime-power full-spark theorem makes every minor with a type-A row or column set nonsingular. After translating a type-B column set to \(\{0,pa,b\}\), a type-B row set gives determinant \((v_2-v_1)(u_3-u_1)\ne0\); a type-C row set makes the first two columns proportional while the third separates the three lifts, so rank is exactly two. Two type-C sets factor as an outer product, giving rank one. Direct counting yields \(B=p^3(p-1)^2/2\) and \(C_3=p^2(p-1)(p-2)/6\), hence the stated totals. An independent p=3 full minor-rank replay agreed with all type predictions.

final_claim: For \(N=p^2\) with \(p\) an odd prime, a three-by-three Fourier minor is singular exactly for type pairs \((C,C),(C,B),(B,C)\) in the record's modulo-\(p\) occupancy classification; these have ranks one, two, two respectively, and the stated exact singular/rank counts follow.
limitations: Only three-by-three minors of the cyclic Fourier matrix at an odd prime square are classified.
